NCAAF
WAKE @ SMU • Sat 12:00pm
SMU -1
-108
Spread
Picked: Nov 11 @ 2:17pm
Analysis
Since SMU joined the ACC in 2024, they are 12-0 at home against conference opponents, with an average margin of victory of nearly 21 points per game. But Wake Forest has won and covered in seven straight games, despite having injury issues with QB Gio Lopez. Here's why I like the Mustangs: outside of a home loss to Miami, where the Hurricanes kind of shut it down in the second half, and a win the next week at Louisville, the Demon Deacons have beaten next to no one. Seven of their eight wins are against teams below .500. Expect more Mustangs home magic on Saturday. SMU 34, Wake Forest 27.
NCAAF
NWEST @ OHIOST • Sat 12:00pm
OHIOST -14
-107
Spread
Picked: Nov 13 @ 9:04am
Analysis
Oregon was supposed to be Ohio State's bounce-back game, but the Buckeyes ran into a buzz saw in the second half. I like them to bounce back at home against a Northwestern team that's spiraling.
With Aidan Childs out, Nico Marcoli struggled against Iowa, posting negative passing EPA, a passing-down success rate below 30% and just 1.67 points per opportunity.
If Northwestern can't move the ball, how does it keep up with this Buckeyes passing attack? Luke Fahey isn't Julian Sayin, but Jeremiah Smith should feast against Montae Pote or Ore Adeyi. Neither is equipped to handle No. 4 as he continues his Heisman campaign.
This feels like a 35-10 Ohio State victory, with some vengeance behind it.
NCAAF
WAKE @ SMU • Sat 12:00pm
WAKE
-105
Money Line
Picked: Nov 13 @ 9:53pm
Analysis
SMU is favored, mostly because they have been unbeatable at home, having won all 12 conference games at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in Dallas since joining the conference prior to the 2024 season. They also have QB Kevin Jennings leading a passing attack that is seventh in the nation, averaging 321.6 yards per game.
However, Wake Forest has the more complete statistical profile, a defense capable of limiting SMU's rushing attack, and an offense that has been difficult to stop. The Demon Deacons have been one of the hottest teams, outscoring their last five opponents 264-31, an average of nearly 53-6 per game. Wake ranks fourth nationally in scoring offense (43.3 PPG), ninth in total offense (487.7 YPG) and 10th in passing (311.9 YPG).
NCAAF
TWST @ RI • Sat 12:00pm
RI
-140
Money Line
Picked: Nov 13 @ 10:49pm
Analysis
This opened at -215 and frankly I thought perhaps should have been higher --- I'm not sure why it has come barreling down. Maybe some Towson person knows something I don't? Is Hank Evans out for RI? (Me, Myself & Irene is about all I know about that state culturally). By all accounts, RI is the better team. Home finale and Senior Day for the Rams. They are two-time defending CAA champions, combining for a 15-1 league record in 2024 and 2025. They aren't that good this year but still should pull this out against the two-win Tigers.
NCAAF
BAMA @ VANDY • Sat 12:45pm
VANDY +14.5
-110
Spread
Picked: Nov 13 @ 6:13pm
Analysis
In its five latest games, Alabama has faced four teams ranked 16th or better on game day, plus Texas A&M highly ranked early in the year. Not that the Crimson Tide will let up against Vandy, but they likely will not be in a blowout frame of mind, especially with QB Keelon Thomas expected to sit at least much of the game with an injury. Austin Mack, who came with Tuscaloosa from Washington with coach Kalen DeBoer, has launched all of four passes this season. The Commodores have regressed from recent seasons but finally notched an SEC win last weekend at Mississippi State. Plauers who were around for Vandy's upset of Bama in 2024 should not lack confidence.

Renner's post-deadline 2027 NFL mock draft: How the trade deadline affected the first three rounds
The Eagles and Titans rebuild after the deadline, while the Chargers land a new weapon for Justin Herbert in Jeremiah Smith
By
Mike Renner
Nov 11, 2026
at
5:57 pm ET
3 min read
Getty Images
Dante Moore, Julian Sayin, LaNorris Sellers, CJ Carr -- what do all three of those quarterbacks have in common? All of them have more years of eligibility. With Sayin and Carr, I think physical development and mastery are needed for them to get drafted where they want to. For Moore, he could use a full healthy season after his scary head injury last weekend. And for Sellers, well, there's a lot that needs to change. I have two of those four returning to school for the sake of this mock, and while Moore and Carr do get selected here, it's very possible both withdraw from hearing their name called this April.
If those four return to school, this "loaded" quarterback class becomes far less exciting. That said, the draft is still loaded at other positions—especially the ones that get paid the big bucks. Three receivers, two offensive tackles, and two edge rushers go within the top 10 of what's shaping up to be a blue-chip-heavy draft class.
That certainly bodes well for teams like the Philadelphia Eagles and Tennessee Titans, who picked up some top-end draft capital in the weeks leading up to the NFL trade deadline. They now join the New York Jets and Cleveland Browns as teams with multiple first-round picks in the 2027 draft. Tennessee, the Atlanta Falcons, and the Arizona Cardinals also picked up second-round picks over the last few weeks. With the dust settled after the deadline, let's take a look at how those new picks are being spent.
One last thing, and this is important: The draft order was determined using the reverse Super Bowl odds at DraftKings Sportsbook. The Jets have three first-round picks: their own, the Cowboys' from the Quinnen Williams trade and the Colts' from the Sauce Gardner trade. The Cowboys have the Packers' selection from the Micah Parsons trade. The Browns have the Rams' first from the Myles Garrett trade. There have also been a total of 18 trades made before the deadline, nine of which involved picks in the first three rounds of this draft.
OK, let's get to it!

College football schedule 2026: What to watch in Week 11, TV channels, streaming, Saturday kickoff times
Week 11 is full of matchups with CFP and conference championship implications
By
Austin Nivison
Nov 13, 2026
at
1:16 pm ET
4 min read
Getty Images
There are only a few weeks left in the college football season, and Week 11 will play a major role in sorting out races for conference titles and the College Football Playoff.
That gets started right away as Wake Forest travels to Dallas for a key ACC matchup against SMU. The Demon Deacons can silence the doubters once and for all with a road win over the Mustangs, and that win might be enough to push them into the playoff field on Tuesday night. Conversely, SMU can take a big step toward Charlotte if it beats Wake Forest.
Later in the afternoon, we'll find out whether its win over Ohio State can propel USC to a playoff run. The Trojans haven't been good on the road in Big Ten play, but this would be a great time to snap that trend. The Hoosiers have been vulnerable for most of the season, although the open date may have served them well.
Finally, Texas goes into Baton Rouge for a primetime showdown against LSU. The Tigers can't afford another loss, so it'll be interesting to see how they play with their backs against the wall. The Longhorns could -- for all intents and purposes -- punch thier CFP ticket with a win.
With so many quality games on all day, we've created a handy guide to help you organize your viewing experience.
The best games
No. 13 Wake Forest at SMU -- 12 p.m. on ESPN,  Fubo (try for free): The Demon Deacons desperately need another quality win for their CFP resume, and beating the Mustangs in Dallas would qualify. SMU just crushed Virginia Tech last week, so it's fully capable of putting a big damper on Wake Forest's Cinderella run. Then again, that same SMU team also lost to Syracuse. Which versions of the Mustangs will we see on Saturday? This matchup also has major ACC championship implications because the winner will help its chances of getting there immensely.
No. 22 Missouri at No. 1 Georgia -- 3:30 p.m on ABC,  Fubo (try for free): This is kind of Missouri's last stand as far as the CFP is concerned. That's not ideal for the Tigers, as they're 1-12 all-time against the Bulldogs and have never beaten the No. 1 team in the country. I guess there's no better time to change that than the present. On the other sideline, Georgia is rolling. The Bulldogs have mauled both of their opponents since the open date, and that latest victory was a dismantling of No. 10 Ole Miss in Oxford. Missouri faces a steep climb to pull off the upset.
No. 18 USC at No. 9 Indiana -- 3:30 p.m. on CBS, CBSSports.com, Paramount+ Premium: Will that win over Ohio State serve as a springboard for the Lincoln Riley era at USC? Did the open date allow Indiana to reset on offense? Those are the two questions I have going into this game. The Trojans have been abhorrent when they have to go eastward in Big Ten play. They just got demolished by Wisconsin a few weeks ago. That said, the Hoosiers have been incredibly vulnerable. They needed overtime to beat Michigan and Minnesota, and the offense has been sputtering. This is a fascinating matchup with immense CFP implications.
No. 2 Utah at No. 23 Arizona -- 7:30 p.m. on Fox,  Fubo (try for free): This has all the makings of a letdown game for Utah. The Utes are coming off a hard-fought rivalry win over BYU, and now they're going on the road to face another top-25 opponent. That exact scenario has tripped up more than a few teams this season. Arizona, meanwhile, narrowly avoided a trap-game loss to TCU last weekend. If the Wildcats are going to beat Utah, Noah Fifita will have to outplay Devon Dampier, and he's capable of doing that. If the Utes get past the Wildcats, they have a clear path to a 12-0 finish.
No. 6 Texas at No. 21 LSU -- 7:30 p.m. on ABC,  Fubo (try for free): Could you imagine the level of angst in Death Valley if LSU gets off to a slow start in this game? The Tigers can't even let doubt creep into anyone's mind because they're one loss away from elimination in the College Football Playoff race. LSU moved the ball well in last week's loss to Alabama, but it struggled to finish drives. That won't get any easier against Texas, which has a strong red-zone defense. The question for the Longhorns is how well they'll hold up on offense. A number of key players are banged up, and that will only make it tougher to operate in a hostile environment.
No. 12 Texas Tech at No. 25 Oklahoma State -- 9:30 p.m. on ESPN,  Fubo (try for free): If you miss the days of Big 12 shootouts, find a way to watch this game. The total is 73.5 points, according to SportsLine, and both offenses are capable of hanging crooked numbers on the board. More importantly, the defenses are more than willing to allow crooked numbers. Thomas Castellanos has ignited the Red Raiders offense, and now he gets to face a porous Cowboys defense. On the other side, Drew Mestemaker keeps working his way up 2027 NFL Draft boards.

Zuffa Boxing 13 start time, fight card, predictions and where to watch Carlos Adames vs. Gerome Warburton
The middleweight champion makes his debut at 168 pounds on Saturday in Saudi Arabia
By
Brent Brookhouse
Nov 13, 2026
at
2:38 pm ET
2 min read
Getty Images
WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames will make his Zuffa Boxing debut on Saturday when he faces Gerome Warburton in the main event of Zuffa Boxing 13 from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Rather than defending his title, Adames will be battling Warburton at super middleweight.
Adames has long been one of the best talents in a struggling middleweight division, making him one of the bigger signings in Zuffa's young history.
In October 2022, Adames defeated Juan Macias Montiel to win the interim WBC title. After successfully defending the interim belt against Julian Williams, Adames was promoted to full champion after Jermall Charlo was stripped of his title.
Sign up for Paramount+ and watch Zuffa Boxing 13 for no additional fee -- along every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Since becoming full champion, Adames has retained the title win a win over Terrell Gausha, a draw against Hamzah Sheeraz and a win over Austin "Ammo" Williams. Adames joins Aaron McKenna, who won the IBF title at Zuffa Boxing 10, as middleweight world champions under Zuffa control.
Warburton is a step down in competition for Adames. Adames is far and away the best fighter Warburton has faced in his career.
Warburton will enter Saturday's fight on a three-fight winning streak since a fourth-round TKO loss to Kieron Conway. Two of those recent victories came against fellow Englishman Nathan Heaney.
Let's take a closer look at the rest of the fight card set for Saturday nightin Saudi Arabia before getting to a prediction and expert pick on the main event below.
Zuffa Boxing 13 fight card
Carlos Adames vs. Gerome Warburton, super middleweights
Andres Teran -125 vs. Jason Moloney -106, bantamweights
Bruno Surace vs. Kamil Bednarek, super middleweights

Ivan Ortiz vs. Dariial Kuchmenov, lightweights

Jakhongir Zokirov vs. Brandon Colantonio, heavyweights
Rayan Awaji vs. Sudais Lubega, welterweights
Abdualaziz Alotebi vs. Ezra Ssaili, featherweights
Prediction
There's not much mystery to how this fight is likely to play out. Adames has been proving himself against elite middleweights for years, while Warburton has not sniffed the world championship level. That's not to take a shot at Warburton, who is a solid B-tier fighter, but rather to set a base level of expectations.
Adames should cruise on Saturday, with the bigger question being how Adames looks moving up a division to super middleweight. It's unlikely Adames sticks at super middle, but it could be a bit of a glimpse into the future.
Adames is a better boxer, better puncher and more experienced at an elite level. Warburton has was stopped by Conway, who has just seven stoppage wins in 23 career victories, after Warburton's corner threw in the towel. There's no reason to expect Adames can't find the finish by attacking the body the same way Conway did. Pick: Carlos Adames via TKO5

A closer look at the top games on tap Saturday as college football Week 11 takes center stage
By
Brandon Marcello
Nov 14, 2026
at
12:41 am ET
3 min read
Getty Images
Lane Kiffin and Steve Sarkisian go way back; their friendship dates back to their time at USC. Their relationship, forged through triumphs and failures, has strengthened in recent years as Sarkisian helped Kiffin work through sobriety and improve his personal life off the field.
On Saturday night, the old friends reunite, each trying to eliminate the other from the College Football Playoff race.
No. 21 LSU, fresh off its first home loss under Kiffin, is trying to avoid dropping home games in consecutive weeks for the first time since 1994. No. 6 Texas has won six straight games against ranked opponents, the longest active streak in the FBS. The loser may very well be eliminated from playoff contention.
It's one of five ranked-on-ranked matchups in a week built for more chaos. A top-two team has lost in five straight weeks, tying 2007 for the longest stretch in AP Top 25 history.
No. 1 Georgia hosts No. 22 Missouri, which has never beaten an AP No. 1 team in 18 tries. No. 2 Utah, one of two unbeaten FBS teams remaining, visits No. 23 Arizona as a slight favorite against the Wildcats. Both of Arizona's wins over top-10 teams since 2015 came against the Utes, and starting quarterback Noah Fifita is 2-0 against them.
On CBS, No. 9 Indiana hosts No. 18 USC, with the Hoosiers fighting for a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game and the Trojans trying to stay alive in the playoff race. Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover is off the injury report, but leading rusher Turbo Richard is out. A loss would all but end USC's playoff hopes.
Meanwhile, No. 12 Texas Tech visits No. 25 Oklahoma State in the Dust Bowl.
Conference races are still in flux, but Georgia can clinch a spot in the final SEC Championship Game on Saturday with a win and some help.
Let's get to our experts' Week 11 picks.
No. 18 USC vs. No. 9 Indiana
7:30 p.m. on CBS  CBSSports.com,  CBS Sports App  Paramount+ Premium: Five of Indiana's six Big Ten games have been decided by a touchdown or less. The only exception was a 47-15 win against an overmatched Rutgers team. The Hoosiers haven't shown the ability to pull away and dominate quality opposition. So long as IU limits catastrophic turnovers, it will win the game on the basis of its physicality on both lines of scrimmage. But it's difficult to envision the Hoosiers suddenly pulling away from a team of USC's caliber. Now in his 32nd season, Michigan State coach Tom Izzo has earned a No. 1 seed for the NCAA Tournament four times in his career, but it has only happened once since 2001 and not at all since 2012. Could this be the year that changes?

UCLA debuted as a No. 9 seed, which was low relative to its standing in preseason metrics. Well, the Bruins proved they deserve to be much higher — for now anyway — when they beat Arizona 84-75 on the season's first night. After that win and two subsequent buy-game wins, the 3-0 Bruins are up to a No. 4 seed in our update. The remainder of UCLA's nonconference schedule is relatively light, but the Arizona win should stand the test of time.
Why isn't UCLA ahead of Arizona? Well, the Wildcats still rank ahead of UCLA in predictive metrics and have huge opportunities against Auburn and UConn coming over the next week. But the Wildcats did drop from a No. 1 seed to a No. 2 seed in this projection. We'll learn more about Tommy Lloyd's club very soon.
While UCLA stands out as a big riser from the Big Ten, Purdue stands out for the opposite reason. After debuting in the preseason as a No. 5 seed, the Boilermakers started 1-2 with losses to Gonzaga and Valparaiso. Purdue is now one of the "Last Four in" and slotted as a No. 12 seed being sent to the "Opening Round." Why didn't they fall out entirely? They are still a top-40 team in predictive metrics, suggesting that a rebound is likely in the cards.
Rematch rules
Amid conference consolidation and tournament expansion, the NCAA has again relaxed rules around rematches. Official NCAA guidance no longer includes a mandate to avoid nonconference rematches in the second round.
While the NCAA will seek to avoid nonconference rematches in the Opening Round and first round, those rules can be relaxed for conferences with more than nine teams in the field. They can also be relaxed if a league has multiple teams among the final 12 at-large teams playing in the Opening Round.
This is how we ended up with the possibility of a first-round game between Tennessee and Florida State. The Volunteers and Seminoles play on Dec. 1, meaning the committee will seek to avoid a potential first-round matchup between them. But the SEC has 13 teams in this projection, and the ACC has two teams playing in the Opening Round.
To avoid violating other bracketing principles, it was easier just to roll with a potential Tennessee/FSU rematch. As for conference rematches, they are allowed to occur as early as the second round between teams that played only once before the NCAA Tournament. But even that can be relaxed for leagues with nine or more teams in the bracket, which the Big 12, Big Ten and SEC each have in this projection.
Full conference breakdown
Here is the full rundown of multi-bid leagues from the latest 76-team CBS Sports Bracketology.

ACC (8): Duke, Virginia, Louisville, Miami, North Carolina, Virginia Tech, NC State, Florida State
Big East (5): UConn, St. J

College football teams scrambling to find alternate travel plans after FAA lifts ground-stop order
The nationwide ground stoppage could have a major impact on Week 11 in college football
By
Austin Nivison
Richard Johnson
Brandon Marcello
Nov 14, 2026
at
1:23 am ET
9 min read
Getty Images
On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stoppage for all departing flights due to " extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety." That announcement came as numerous college football programs were preparing to leave for road games across the country.
After a lengthy halt to all air travel, the FAA lifted the ground stop on Friday night, but programs still have work to do in order to finalize their travel plans. In his press conference, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy recommended that schools reach out to the FAA about their travel arrangements.
"I would encourage those football teams to reach out to the FAA to schedule their flight times and make sure they have games going off tomorrow," Duffy said.
As of Friday night, there were quite a few teams that haven't taken off, and they are still working on alternative travel plans. That raises another set of questions, including timing and player safety. What if these teams can't get the proper rest after spending most of Friday night on a bus, and will games have to be pushed back due to late arrivals?
Another wrinkle in all this is that on-air talent and behind-the-scenes staff for broadcasts will be affected by the groundstop. That will be something else to monitor as the chaos unfolds.
As teams and conferences sort out the next steps, here is the latest on how notable Week 11 matchups have been affected by the FAA's groundstop, including these changes to kickoff times as of Friday night (all times ET):

UFC returns to Madison Square Garden on Saturday. For 10 years, the famed New York City venue has become a regular destination for the mixed martial arts leader. UFC 334 is a worthy successor with its championship double-header.
Ciryl Gane makes his first UFC heavyweight title defense against Josh Hokit in the main event. Their paths to the title couldn't be more different, with Gane having more chances than most. Gane failed to capture the title from Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones and Tom Aspinall -- a murderer's row -- before finally becoming undisputed champion by beating Alex Pereira in an interim title fight and later being promoted.
Speaking of Pereira, who likely has no desire to be compared to Hokit, there's an interesting throughline between them. Both men spent exactly 371 days between their UFC debuts and their first title shots. What's more, both those title shots are hosted in MSG. Hokit's ability to draw attention and his collegiate wrestling background have helped narrow the betting gap between him and Gane in the leadup to the fight.

Oddsmakers are even less certain about the co-main event. Women's bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison defends her title against the greatest women's MMA fighter of all time, Amanda Nunes. The many mysteries surrounding the fight, including Harrison's recent neck surgery and Nunes' 41-month layoff, make it hard to predict how each fighter will be.

Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit predictions
Campbell: As it has been with most UFC title fights involving Gane, his level of success will likely be dictated by his ability to keep his back off of the canvas, especially against a former NCAA Division I All-American wrestler in Hokit. But Gane, who now trains out of Dubai, has put in the work to improve his takedown defense and the longer he can keep this a kickboxing match against the aggressive but still inexperienced Hokit, the more the odds begin to favor him. For whatever Hokit lacks in size or seasoned technique, he typically makes up for with speed and aggression. But Gane is the rare heavyweight who can match his athleticism and cardio, which means the first French-born UFC champion's overall experience advantage should be the difference in the championship rounds.
Brookhouse: Gane has considerable advantages in size and striking technique. As impressive as Hokit's grit was in his war with Curtis Blaydes, Blaydes isn't a technical striker on the level Gane is. That kind of face-first aggression is what a striker like Gane loves to see and punish. Hokit has good speed and is very aggressive, but if he can't get Gane to the ground consistently and hold him there, I have trouble seeing a path to victory for him.
Mahjouri: I think the odds should be wider. I really struggle to see a path to victory for Hokit. Most people will say it's his wrestling; after all, he's an NCAA Division I All-American. But I think people are holding on too tightly to Gane's struggles against Jon Jones and Francis Ngannou. It's been more than three years since he imploded against them. Hokit's success largely comes down to his athleticism and heart. He's more agile than many lumbering heavyweights and is fearless in his pursuit.
